messages.author: 4076f5688b45a1a5
messages.subject: Problems with pardiso library
parts:
Hi everyone!
I am sorry to bother you for problems with pardiso, but they are not answering my mail so I thought I could ask you. Some time ago I downloaded the licence for R-INLA and it worked fine on my virtual machine. Now, it stopped working and I have no idea why.
I'm trying to understand why and how I can make it work again because the computation times are too high now. I precise that I'm running the Rscript on a virtual machine on ubuntu. What I did, and didn't work, is the following:
Went to https://pardiso-project.org/r-inla/ and downloaded the License, using the university email and setting as username the one on the Virtual Machine (typing whoami on the terminal of ubuntu after loggin in the VM with ssh command)
Got the licence code and wrote it on a note file, saved as pardiso.lic.
Put this file in the VM at /home/dalla  and specified the remote location (the place in the VM) with:
library(INLA)
inla.setOption(pardiso.license = "/home/dalla/pardiso.lic")

Then, when running the script it does not recognize the licence, and the output is:

[PARDISO] License error. Wrong user license.
[PARDISO] Please obtain a new license at www.pardiso-project.org/r-inla

[PARDISO] user name: dalla
[PARDISO] directory: /home/dalla
....
parse section=[15] name=[INLA.pardiso] type=[PARDISO]
    inla_parse_pardiso...
        section[INLA.pardiso]
        verbose[0]
        debug[0]
        parallel.reordering[1]
        nrhs[-1]
Thank you very much in advance, and again I'm sorry to bother you on this question.
Alessandro

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problems with pardiso library
parts:
/The pardiso license is valid for a year hence if your license isn't expired then you specified the wrong file path.

I have experienced similar issue in the past. l am using Ubuntu via WSL. 

You should try changing the license path by moving it to another folder e.g. /mnt/d/xxx/pardiso.lic

messages.author: 386ba2ce7aee385c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problems with pardiso library
parts:
This issue is not normal. Try:

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(smtp="pardiso", pardiso.license="~/pardiso.lic")
inla.pardiso.check()

The output message is:
[1] "SUCCESS: PARDISO IS INSTALLED AND WORKING"

if you don't obtain this output, request another license and set it in the home folder on your server with the .lic file.

Erick

messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Re: Problems with pardiso library
parts:
Hi  Alessandro,

I'm sorry for not getting back to you sooner. I replicated your problem with the pardiso license. The problem is not the folder or the directory. It is the file extension. What file editor did you use in saving the license. If it was notepad or a text editor, try this (or add .txt to the license file name)

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(pardiso.license = "/home/dalla/pardiso.lic.txt")
inla.pardiso.check()


I tried without the .txt extension and I had the error you had earlier which I also had some time ago. let me know if this works.

regards,

messages.author: a96aa45411c16ae6
messages.subject: Re: Problems with pardiso library
parts:
Hello,
I would suggest you adding a line break after your license code.
You just need to press return (enter) at the end of the license code line then save.
Every year I face this problem and adding a line break always worked.

Best,
